narrative.feedback:
Your Leadership Profile: The Energiser

Your dominant colour is YELLOW — Collaborative. You consistently chose to bring people with you. Your decisions favoured open dialogue, shared ownership and the morale of the team, even when a faster unilateral call was available. This was driven by your two most-used styles: democratic (29%) and authoritative (26%). Your signature strengths are you built buy-in before you acted, you kept the team energised through setbacks, and you made it safe for people to raise ideas. The edge to watch is avoiding the hard, unpopular call, and letting consensus delay a decision that was yours to make. For example, in year-end reckoning you leaned on democratic leadership — one of the moments that shaped the profile above.

Self-Image vs Reality:

✅ Aligned. You told us you lead with Democratic — and your decisions bore that out, using it 29% of the time, more than any other style. Your self-perception and your behaviour are telling the same story, which is the foundation of coachable leadership.

What You Did Well:

You achieved exceptional growth (28.0%) while maintaining team performance. Your team morale remained strong, demonstrating that you brought people with you. You showed genuine agility, particularly in adapting your approach when faced with challenges.

Your LEAD Competencies Explained:

Leadership (43%): Adequate - Limited style variety suggests some over-reliance on comfort zone.

Excellence (27%): Needs development - 0 info requests indicates decisions made on instinct rather than evidence.

Agility (30%): Needs development - Difficulty adapting to uncertainty or changing contexts.

Determination (24%): Needs development - Insufficient drive for results or resilience under pressure.

Decision-Making Rigor:

⚠️ You requested zero additional information across all 9 scenarios. This "decide on instinct" approach is fast but dangerous - you are operating with incomplete data. You succeeded despite this, but will not always be lucky. Evidence-based leaders outperform gut-decision makers over time.

Your Leadership Personality (Jung Model):

Your dominant color is YELLOW: Optimistic, enthusiastic, collaborative. You repeatedly chose to bring people with you and keep the team energised.

Typical YELLOW strengths: High Leadership (collaborative), High Agility (adaptable), energizing teams. Watch out for: Lower Determination (conflict avoidance), scattered focus. ✅ This matches your profile - great people skills but could be more results-focused when needed.

The Key Insight:

You demonstrated balanced leadership, adapting your style to context while keeping both results and people in focus. This is sustainable high performance.

narrative.feedback:
Your Leadership Profile: The Adaptive Leader

Your dominant colour is BALANCED — Adaptive Leader. You consistently chose the approach the moment demanded. No single style dominated your decisions, and you moved between driving, analysing, energising and developing as the situation changed. This was driven by your two most-used styles: coaching (22%) and affiliative (21%). Your signature strengths are you matched your approach to the moment, you drew on a wide range of styles, and you adapted when the context shifted rather than repeating one play. The edge to watch is range without a signature — being everything to everyone can read as having no clear centre. For example, in difficult conversation you leaned on coaching leadership — one of the moments that shaped the profile above.

Self-Image vs Reality:

⚠️ A gap worth examining. You identified yourself as Authoritative, but your decisions used it only 19% of the time. What actually drove your play was coaching (22%). This is a significant gap. You may be leading from a style you do not fully recognise — which means the impact you intend and the impact you create are not yet the same thing. That is not a character flaw; it is the single most useful thing this profile can tell you. Seek candid feedback from people who experience your leadership daily. Neither style is "wrong" — the goal is to close the distance between how you see yourself and how you actually behave, because self-aware leaders develop faster.

What You Did Well:

You successfully achieved 16.8% growth and met your target. Your team morale remained strong, demonstrating that you brought people with you. You showed genuine agility, particularly in adapting your approach when faced with challenges.

Your LEAD Competencies Explained:

Leadership (45%): Adequate - Limited style variety suggests some over-reliance on comfort zone.

Excellence (48%): Adequate - Only 7 info requests suggests some reliance on gut-feel decision making.

Agility (52%): Adequate - Struggled somewhat with ambiguous situations or changing priorities.

Determination (9%): Needs development - Insufficient drive for results or resilience under pressure.

Decision-Making Rigor:

Good: You requested information 7 times (moderate thoroughness). You balance speed with due diligence. Consider: did you request info on the right decisions - the high-stakes, irreversible ones?

Where You Left Performance on the Table:

You achieved 16.8% when 30%+ was possible with more strategic choices.

Your Leadership Personality (Jung Model):

Your dominant color is BALANCED: The Adaptive Leader - You repeatedly chose the approach the moment demanded rather than one fixed style.

Balanced Leadership Profile: You do not show a strong preference for any single Jung temperament. That said, you lean slightly towards YELLOW - not enough to dominate your profile, but it is the colour you return to most often. This suggests high adaptability - you can shift between different leadership modes as context requires. Your LEAD scores likely show relatively even development across all four dimensions.

The Key Insight:

You have strong leadership instincts. The next level is consciously adapting your style to what each situation requires, rather than defaulting to your comfort zone.
